stem: ‘Satkaryavada’ is the main doctrine of which philosophical system?
expl: In the context of cause and eff ect, the doctrine of Satkaryavada belongs to the Sankhya philosophy. According to Sankhya Darshan, there is an inseparable relationship between cause and eff ect, meaning that the eff ect pre-exists in the cause and is manifested from it. The absence of a cause leads to the non-existence of its eff ect. This type of relationship between cause and eff ect is called an inseparable connection (Avinabhava), meaning that the existence of one necessarily implies the existence of the other. If one does not exist, the other cannot exist either. The existence of one entity is always dependent on the existence of another. For example, if there is no clay, a pot cannot be created.

stem: The Chalukyan ruler Pulakesin's victory over Harsha was in the year –
expl: Harsha's southward march was stopped on Narmada river by the Chalukya king Pulakesin who ruled over a great part of modern Karnataka and Maharashtra with his capital at Badami in the modern Bijapur district of Karnataka. The battle between Harsha and Pulakesin was fought sometime between 630 to 634 AD. The fi rst reason in support of this battle is the result of the battle of Vallabhi which itself cannot be said to have been fought before 630 AD. Again Pulakesin's lohnara inscription of 630 AD which mentions the names of his defeated enemies, does not include the name of Harsha, but Aihole inscription of 634 AD mentions this battle. In these conditions, the correct timing would be between 630 AD and 634 AD, so the nearest answer can be option (d). In April 2016, researchers from the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute claimed that the date of Pulakesin's great triumph over Harsha could be fi xed at 618 AD.
